English

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

camisa (plural camisas or camisae)

  1. Alternative form of camisia.

See also

[edit]
  • camisa de chino

Aragonese

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

    Inherited from Late Latin camisia.

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • IPA(key): /kaˈmisa/
    • Syllabification: ca‧mi‧sa
    • Rhymes: -isa

    Noun

    [edit]

    camisa f (plural camisas)

    1. shirt

    References

    [edit]
    • “camisa”, in Aragonario, diccionario aragonés–castellano (in Spanish)
    • “camisa”, in Diccionario ortografico de l’aragonés (seguntes la PO de l’EFA)‎[1], Zaragoza: EDACAR, 2023, →ISSN
    • Bal Palazios, Santiago (2002), “camisa”, in Dizionario breu de a luenga aragonesa, Zaragoza, →ISBN

    Asturian

    [edit]
    Asturian Wikipedia has an article on:
    camisa
    Wikipedia ast

    Etymology

    [edit]

    From Old Leonese, from Late Latin camisia, from Proto-West Germanic *hamiþi.

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • IPA(key): /kaˈmisa/ [kaˈmi.sa]
    • Rhymes: -isa
    • Syllabification: ca‧mi‧sa

    Noun

    [edit]

    camisa f (plural camises)

    1. shirt

    Derived terms

    [edit]
    • camiseta

    Further reading

    [edit]
    • “camisa”, in Diccionariu de la llingua asturiana [Dictionary of the Asturian Language] (in Asturian), 1st edition, Academy of the Asturian Language [Asturian: Academia de la Llingua Asturiana], 2000, →ISBN
    • Xosé Lluis García Arias (2002–2004), “camisa”, in Diccionario general de la lengua asturiana [General Dictionary of the Asturian Language] (in Spanish), Editorial Prensa Asturiana, →ISBN

    Catalan

    [edit]
    Catalan Wikipedia has an article on:
    camisa
    Wikipedia ca

    Etymology

    [edit]

    Inherited from Late Latin camisia (compare Occitan camisa or chamisa, French chemise, Spanish camisa), from Proto-West Germanic *hamiþi.

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • IPA(key): (Central, Balearic) [kəˈmi.zə]
    • IPA(key): (Valencia) [kaˈmi.za]
    • Audio (Catalonia):(file)

    Noun

    [edit]

    camisa f (plural camises)

    1. shirt, blouse
    2. folder
    3. dust jacket
      Synonym: sobrecoberta
    4. jacket (outer shell of a bullet)
    5. (automotive) cylinder sleeve
    6. (castells, informal) a casteller who has been formally accepted as a member of a colla
    7. (lighting) mantle
      Synonym: camiseta

    Derived terms

    [edit]
    • aixecar la camisa
    • camisa d'assaig
    • camisa de dormir
    • camisa de força
    • camiseta
    • deixar sense camisa
    • encamisar

    References

    [edit]
    • “camisa” in Diccionari català-valencià-balear, Antoni Maria Alcover and Francesc de Borja Moll, 1962.

      Galician

      [edit]

      Etymology

      [edit]

        Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese camisa.

        Pronunciation

        [edit]

        • Rhymes: -isa
        • Hyphenation: ca‧mi‧sa

        Noun

        [edit]

        camisa f (plural camisas)

        1. shirt
          Synonyms: chambra, blusa, cos, envestidoiro
        2. shedding (of a snake)

        Related terms

        • camisola
        • camisón
        • escamisar

        • Antón Luís Santamarina Fernández, Ernesto Xosé González Seoane, María Álvarez de la Granja, editors (2003–2018), “camisa”, in Tesouro informatizado da lingua galega (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega

        Old Galician-Portuguese

        [edit]

        Alternative forms

        [edit]
        • camjsa, camjssa

        Etymology

        [edit]

          Inherited from Late Latin camisia.

          Pronunciation

          [edit]
          • IPA(key): /kaˈmiza/
          • Rhymes: -iza
          • Hyphenation: ca‧mi‧sa

          Noun

          [edit]

          camisa f (plural camisas)

          1. shirt (article of clothing)
            • 13th century, Estêvão da Guarda, Pois a todos avorrece; republished as Angelo Colocci, compiler, Cancioneiro da Biblioteca Nacional, Italy, c. 1525–1526, cantiga 1306:
              ela t(ra)ge camiſa / De ſirgo
              she's wearing a silk shirt

          Descendants

          [edit]
          • Fala: camisa, camisha (Lagarteiru, Mañegu)
          • Galician: camisa
          • Portuguese: camisa (see there for further descendants)

          References

          [edit]
          • Ferreiro, Manuel (2014–2026), “camisa”, in Universo Cantigas: edición crítica da poesía medieval galego-portuguesa [Universo Cantigas: critical edition of Galician-Portuguese medieval poetry] (in Galician), A Coruña: University of A Coruña, →ISSN
          • Seoane, Ernesto Xosé González; Granja, María Álvarez de la; Agrelo, Ana Isabel Boullón (2006–2022), “cam@sa”, in Dicionario de Dicionarios do galego medieval [Dictionary of dictionaries of Medieval Galician] (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega
          • Barreiro, Xavier Varela; Guinovart, Xavier Gómez (2006–2018), “camisa”, in Corpus Xelmírez: corpus lingüístico da Galicia medieval [Corpus Xelmírez: linguistic corpus of Medieval Galicia] (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega
          • Cunha, Antônio Geraldo da (2020–2026), “camisa”, in Vocabulário histórico-cronológico do português medieval [Historical and chronological vocabulary of Medieval Portuguese] (in Portuguese), Rio de Janeiro: Fundação Casa de Rui Barbosa

          Old Spanish

          [edit]

          Etymology

          [edit]

            Inherited from Late Latin camisia.

            Pronunciation

            [edit]
            • IPA(key): /kaˈmiza/

            Noun

            [edit]

            camisa f (plural camisas)

            1. shirt
              • 1140-1207, El Cantar de mio Cid (The Song of my Lord), 72r, 3612-3638: Cantar de mio Cid
                el belmez con la camisa e con la guarnizón
                the padded tunic with the shirt and gambleston

            Descendants

            [edit]
            • Ladino: kamisa
            • Spanish: camisa (see there for further descendants)

            Portuguese

            [edit]
            Portuguese Wikipedia has an article on:
            camisa
            Wikipedia pt

            Etymology

            [edit]

              Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese camisa.

              Pronunciation

              [edit]
               
              • (Brazil) IPA(key): /kaˈmi.zɐ/
              • (Brazil) IPA(key): /kaˈmi.zɐ/
                • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /kaˈmi.za/
              • (Portugal) IPA(key): /kɐˈmi.zɐ/

              • Audio (Portugal (Porto)):(file)
              • Rhymes: -izɐ
              • Hyphenation: ca‧mi‧sa

              Noun

              [edit]

              camisa f (plural camisas)

              2. shirt (light garment worn over the torso)
              4. (Brazil) chemise; nightgown (garment mainly worn by women for sleeping in)
                Synonym: (Brazil) camisola
              6. coat; hood (protective cover of an object)
                Synonyms: capa, invólucro

              Derived terms

              [edit]
              • camisa-verde
              • camisinha
              • camisola
              • rasgar a camisa
              • vestir a camisa

              Related terms

              [edit]
              • camiseta

              Descendants

              [edit]
              • Guinea-Bissau Creole: kamisa
              • Kabuverdianu: kamisa, kamiza
              • Korlai Creole Portuguese: kamidz
              • Kristang: kameza
              • Principense: kamiza
              • Sãotomense: kaminza
              • Sranan Tongo: kamisa
                • Aukan: kamísa
                • Saramaccan: kamísa
                • → Dutch: kamisa
              Borrowings

                • Nheengatu: kamixá
              • → Malay: kemeja
                • Indonesian: kemeja
              • → Malayalam: കമീസ് (kamīsŭ)
              • → Telugu: కమీజు (kamīju)
              • → Tetum: kamiza
              • → Urubú-Kaapor: kamixa

                • IPA(key): /kaˈmisa/ [kaˈmi.sa]

                Noun

                camisa f (plural camisas)

                2. gas mantle
                3. (colloquial, El Salvador) condom
